name: Home energy auditor

pf.license.need: Where the state, a utility program or the business's own rules require it, each auditor holds a current energy auditor or building performance credential (a building analyst or rater certification), and the company holds its own registration or contractor license. Some states license nobody: then registration only. Combustion safety testing needs an auditor trained for it.
pf.license.ask: Each auditor's credential name and number. The company's registration or license number, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: Each auditor holds their own credential. The company holds its own registration where the state asks. A new-home energy rating is done only by a certified rater.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Where the state requires licensed or certified auditors: no audit is offered until the company's and the auditor's numbers check out. A rating is offered only with a certified rater.
pf.license.insurance_bond: General liability insurance where the state's form requires it. Shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word. The auditor spends hours inside the home.
pf.license.shown_to_customers: The auditor's credential or license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.not_this_work: Installing insulation, air sealing, heating or cooling equipment, windows or solar, and filing rebate paperwork. They are other businesses' work, never booked under the auditor's plug-in. An auditor never sells the upgrades they recommend at a home they audited.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: one audit visit at the home, priced by the home's size, with a written report later.

list.name: Home energy audit
list.price_kind: set by the customer's answers (square feet, house or condo, year built)

list.length: about 3 hours on site: a blower door test, an infrared scan, a duct check and a combustion safety test, then a results walk-through; the report follows in about 3 business days
list.where: at the home; an adult stays for the whole visit
list.money: card saved at booking; charged at DONE

list.money: card saved at booking; charged at DONE

pf.services.start_times: Set starts, like 8:00am and 1:00pm. The results walk-through comes at the end of the visit.
pf.services.notice: 2 days' notice by default. A sooner time only if Sam says yes.
pf.services.capacity: One auditor per audit. A rating only with a certified rater.
pf.services.nobody_home: No: an adult (18 or older) stays for the whole visit, because the tests run in every room and the heating system is used.
pf.services.online: Report walk-throughs and upgrade plans can be done by video.
pf.services.not_offered: Installing upgrades, filing rebate or incentive paperwork, home inspections, and any promise of savings.
pf.services.partner_work: None. Rosie never names or refers an installer.

before_times: The town or ZIP, and the kind of home: a house, a condo or townhouse, or several units
About how many square feet, and the year built
What bothers you: drafts, hot or cold rooms, high bills, a damp attic or crawl space
How it is heated and cooled: gas, oil, electric or a heat pump, if you know
Do you own the home or rent it?
after_a_time: Pets at the home, and where they'll be
Can an adult stay for the whole visit, about 3 hours?
Is there a wood stove, a fireplace or a gas appliance we should know about?
Will you come for the results walk-through at the end?
secure_page_only: The utility account number and the last 12 months of bills
Photos of the furnace, water heater and attic hatch
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult 18 or older who owns the home, or a tenant. A tenant gives the landlord's yes for any area the tenant cannot enter, like a shared attic or a boiler room; those areas are left out and listed as not tested. An adult must stay for the whole visit.

what_happens: A gas smell, sparks, smoke or a carbon monoxide alarm: whoever is there gets out first, then calls 911 and the gas company from outside. No booking until the home is safe.

Live wires hanging down or flooding up to the outlets: stay away from that area, and call 911 if anyone is in danger. The audit can be booked for the rest of the home; the auditor will not enter that area.

At the visit, a combustion safety test that shows dangerous carbon monoxide or backdrafting stops the test: the auditor tells the household to open windows and leave if needed, and gives 911 and the gas company. The audit goes on only when it is safe.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for gas, sparks, smoke or a carbon monoxide alarm. Yes, with the unsafe area left out, for live wires or flooding.

pf.first_steps.access: An adult stays for the whole visit and lets the auditor into every room, the attic, the crawl space or basement, and the heating system.
pf.first_steps.documents: The last 12 months of energy bills, added on the secure page, if you have them.
prep_for_reminder: Last 12 months of energy bills on the secure page
Clear the way to the attic hatch, crawl space or basement, furnace, water heater and electrical panel
No fire in a fireplace or wood stove for 24 hours before, and the ashes cleaned out
Pets put away, and windows and doors closed
Leave the thermostat where you normally keep it

pf.visit.check_in: The adult at home gives the check-in code to the auditor at the door. The code and DONE confirm the visit.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Nothing is left unlocked: the adult at home opens the door.
pf.visit.what_is_checked: A blower door test of the whole house, an infrared scan of walls and ceilings, a duct check, a combustion safety test of gas and oil appliances, and the attic, walls, windows, doors and lighting, with photos.
pf.visit.not_tested: Anything that can't be reached or safely tested, like a closed-off crawl space or a suspect attic insulation, is listed as not tested. A return visit is offered for the trip fee, with the client's OK.
pf.visit.walk_through: A results walk-through at the end: where air leaks and heat escapes, and the safety readings. Savings and rebates are in the report; nothing is promised on the spot.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An add-on (a duct leakage test, a crawl space moisture check) only if the client says yes first, priced before it is done. The fee never depends on the upgrades the client buys.
pf.visit.proof_done: The check-in code at the start and DONE from the auditor's phone, with photos. The report follows by the date promised.
pf.visit.report: An energy report with ranked upgrades and estimated savings, sent on a secure link by the date promised at booking (the example: 3 business days). Rosie tracks the date.
pf.visit.report_release: Sam picks per service: the report goes out at once, or once the bill is paid. Where the state's rules forbid holding a report, it goes out at once.

pf.money.start: Audits: a card saved at booking, charged at DONE. Walk-throughs and plans at the office: a card saved for the fee, paid at the office after.
pf.money.other_ways: Nothing taken and the bill texted after; paid in full when booking (a test-out); a deposit and the rest on the bill for a multi-unit building quoted first.
pf.money.deposits: None by default on a set-price audit. A multi-unit building quoted from details may take a deposit; the cap, if any, comes from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel, or no way in at the start time: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89). A return visit when part of the home could not be tested: the trip fee. Sam confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.fee_rule: The fee never depends on the upgrades the client buys, the rebates the client gets, or the savings found.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes audit services, from the state form.

never_in_texts: The street address in a first text to someone new
The utility account number and the bills: only the secure link
Findings, photos and the report: only the secure link
pf.messages.who_gets_texts: The client, and the adult who stays at the home only after their own yes.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books, and an adult 18 or older must be home for the visit.

skills: Report walk-throughs and upgrade plans at the office
pf.staff.licenses: Each auditor's own credential, where the state, a program or the business requires it. Ratings only by a certified rater.
pf.staff.stand_in: Another auditor with the same credential and skills may stand in, with the client's OK first.
pf.staff.supervision: A trainee audits only with a credentialed auditor on the job, where the rules allow trainees.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500 and every fee. Pat, the office manager, may too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.fee_independence: The audit fee can't depend on the upgrades the client buys or the rebates the client gets.
pf.rules.no_upgrade_sales: No upgrade or installation work at a home this business audited, for the time the state's rules set. Sam can keep it as the business's own rule anywhere.
pf.rules.report_deadline: The report reaches the client by the date promised at booking. A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.rules.weather: A blower door test needs light wind, and an infrared scan needs a wide gap between inside and outside air. The visit moves to the next good day with no fee.
pf.rules.license_shown: The credential or license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 5 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the report, the readings and the photos.

matter_most: Wind or a small temperature gap makes the tests unreliable: the visit moves to the next good day, with no fee.
A combustion safety test shows dangerous carbon monoxide or backdrafting: the test stops, the household is told to open windows and leave if needed, and 911 and the gas company are given.
The adult at home has to leave, or nobody answers the door: the visit is a no-show only after the safety check and a call; the trip fee is Sam's to confirm.
A fireplace or wood stove was burning, or the ashes were not cleaned out: the blower door test is skipped, listed as not tested, and a return visit is offered for the trip fee.
An area can't be reached or safely tested (a closed-off crawl space, suspect attic insulation): it is listed as not tested.
A tenant can't enter a shared area: it is left out unless the landlord says yes.
The client asks the auditor to install the upgrades: Rosie says this business doesn't do installs at a home it audited.
The client asks for rebate paperwork: Rosie says this business doesn't file it; the report lists the upgrades.
The report runs late: the client hears the new date before the old one passes.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Kept words: 'Trip fee' (the $89 fee for a late cancel or no way in, the parent's word too), 'Grace' (the master's grace time), 'leak' and 'color' (the master's shared safety and fairness lines, S13-40 lists color among protected traits).
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch S1, Tue Oct 27 2026), started from the refitted inspector overlay (set 'from'): an energy audit is a set visit at the home with a written report later, like an inspection. It differs on purpose: an adult stays for the whole visit (the blower door, the infrared scan and the combustion test run in every room), so the parent's lockbox, agent-access and signed-agreement steps are not carried and the master's own check-in stands (the code at the door). The 'Nobody needs to be home' branch of B8-03 is off.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Energy Audits (home energy audits of houses, condos and small multi-unit buildings, with new-home energy ratings as the second kind of work, done only by a certified rater). Flow A is Lee Energy Office, Sam's office: a 30-minute report walk-through, bill review, upgrade lists and a whole-house upgrade plan, at the office, by video or at the home.
Prices are the example business's own: home energy audit $349 (house up to 2,500 sq ft), condo $249, test-out after upgrades $150 (paid in full), duct leakage test $199 ($249 when Sam goes), crawl space moisture check $160, a multi-unit building quoted from the listing and bills at $640 (Sam OKs over $500), trip fee $89. Flow A: report walk-through $35, bill review $20, upgrade priority list $40, second opinion on an audit $55, whole-house upgrade plan $140, at the home $75.
Money, flow B: main list|card|card (a card saved at booking, charged at DONE), list|none|bill (the bill after; the report goes out once it is paid), list|full|none (a test-out paid in full), photos|deposit|bill (a multi-unit building quoted first: $160 deposit, $480 on the bill). Flow A: list|card|counter (main), list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|card|card. No visit-priced path: the fee never depends on the upgrades bought, the rebates won or the savings found.
Who must not be booked (pf.questions, pf.safety): anyone under 18; a home with a gas smell, smoke or sparks or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding (no booking until safe); a home where no adult can stay the whole visit (the audit needs one); a tenant for areas the landlord has not OK'd (left out, listed as not tested). Installation work and rebate paperwork are not offered.
Danger words (pf.safety): a gas smell, sparks or smoke, a carbon monoxide alarm (no booking until safe); live wires hanging down and flooding up to the outlets (booking goes on, that area left out). At the visit, a combustion safety test showing dangerous carbon monoxide ends the test (B8-29 more line). The danger-first call (B3-11, B3-18) uses water up to the outlets, so the two steps read as one conversation. 'High bills', 'drafts' and 'a cold room' are the everyday reasons to book and are not stop words.
Settings: arrive a set start (8:00am and 1:00pm), cutoff 6pm the day before; booking choices limited to a set time. Nothing is sent now. Weather (wind, a small temperature gap) moves the visit with no fee (pf.rules, S13-56). The fact `documents` is not listed, so the master's signed-contract branch is hidden and 'No contract needed' stands.
Rename pairs: only the inspector's pairs that match the frozen master were kept and re-worded for energy audits; addresses and credential numbers are made up (EX-1042 style). The master's 'Leak repair' sign-up row reads 'Large property evaluation' (priced at the visit by size). The report date in the examples is the next day (Fri Oct 23) like the parent's; the real turnaround is the owner's setting (the plug-in's example: 3 business days).
For the verifier: an adult staying the whole visit is my reading of how audits run (the blower door test needs the auditor to move through every room); a business that lets an auditor in with a lockbox would need the parent's design instead. The credential name is generic on purpose.
